briefing.opening: Good morning. Welcome to the climate briefing for September 23, 2026. Today, we have a wide range of news, from climate change denial to escalating warnings about the climate crisis, and various domestic and international efforts to overcome it.

sections.title: 🔴 The Shadow of Climate Change Denial Cast Over the International Community
sections.content: Today at the UN General Assembly, former President Donald Trump once again propagated 'climate change denial,' fostering skepticism about international climate cooperation [1, 89]. He asserted that 'the climate crisis is a hoax,' prompting critical responses from African leaders, the UN Secretary-General, and other heads of state worldwide [89]. Such political obstacles, coupled with the decreasing mention of worsening climate change in Nevada, raise concerns that they could undermine the urgency of climate action [94].

sections.title: ⚠️ Nature's Warning: Escalating Climate Crisis Phenomena
sections.content: The recent appearance of the shark 'Bukang-i' in Busan's North Port is being interpreted as a warning of climate change, drawing both domestic and international attention [2, 4, 7, 21, 90]. This aligns with the phenomenon of tropical animals being found in unusual northern regions, directly demonstrating the impact of climate change on ecosystems [101]. Meanwhile, globally, climate change-induced disasters are intensifying, with a major flood warning in Nepal leading to a complex disaster [5], and an increased risk of landslides in the Southern Appalachians [93]. Australian researchers, in particular, urged faster greenhouse gas reductions, stating that climate inequality would persist for a long time even if carbon neutrality is achieved [6].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Accelerating Domestic and International Climate Change Response and Carbon Neutrality Efforts
sections.content: Amidst the climate crisis, various response efforts are continuing both domestically and internationally. The Korea Rural Community Corporation agreed to cooperate with Taiwan on AI-based water management and climate change response [11, 15, 16], and Seoul's Seongdong-gu announced plans to create climate-resilient gardens [12]. The National Assembly Climate Change Forum held a 2040 post-coal policy discussion, hearing presentations from experts [3], and the Korea Association for Industrial Intelligence and Hope Friends Famine Relief successfully concluded a climate change response project competition, discovering climate action ideas from young people [9, 10]. Furthermore, President Lee, in his UN keynote speech, presented the 'K-Initiative Solution' for AI, climate change, and energy supply chains, expressing his commitment to contributing to the international community [13]. Europe is also expected to spend billions of dollars on climate change adaptation [92, 99], and Japan announced that it can achieve both climate change countermeasures and economic growth simultaneously, demonstrating ongoing global efforts [100].

sections.title: 🌱 Current Status of Renewable Energy Transition and Carbon Neutrality Implementation
sections.content: Efforts to transition to renewable energy for achieving carbon neutrality are ongoing. The new president of the Korea Institute of Energy Research emphasized a major R&D transformation for carbon neutrality, pledging technological leadership [50, 59], and in Australia, renewable energy met 80% of grid demand, reaching an all-time high [63]. KEPCO KPS made its first overseas renewable energy investment by acquiring a stake in an Indonesian hydropower plant, contributing to global renewable energy expansion [74, 75, 81, 83, 84, 85]. Domestic local governments are also expanding their efforts for carbon neutrality, with Gwangyang City receiving the Grand Prize for excellent carbon neutrality administrative practices [29, 45], and Gimhae City being selected as a leading example of local government carbon neutrality [43]. However, challenges remain, including the shortage of personnel in the renewable energy sector [69], the tendency for carbon neutrality practices to be neglected during autumn festival periods [46], and the OECD's warning that steel oversupply could hinder the achievement of carbon neutrality goals [48].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the escalating warnings of the climate crisis amidst the obstacle of climate change denial, as well as the multifaceted domestic and international efforts to overcome it. Only sustained interest and participation can safeguard the future for all of us. This concludes today's climate briefing.
